instructions:
job-service runs jobs: a job is a named script in a repo's jobs.toml, a run one execution of it at one commit, claimed by a runner whose labels and free memory fit.

- A run is submitted pending, claimed and running, and ends succeeded, failed or canceled with its exit code.
- A run's log is read from a byte offset: get_run_log answers the bytes from offset, the log's size, and the run's state, so call it again from offset + the bytes read until the state has ended.
- cancel_run ends a pending run at once; a running one is canceled by its runner shortly after.
- Every tool takes the submitters' token this server was connected with. Registering runners and their claims and reports are the runner protocol, not tools.

tools.name: submit_run
tools.title: Submit a run
tools.description: One run, stored `pending` until a runner whose labels and free memory fit claims it, with what it was for when `for` says. Nothing is checked against the repo here: a run of a job missing from `jobs.toml` at that commit fails on its runner, saying so in its log.

commit.description: The commit to run, as a full lowercase sha: the runner checks out exactly this.

job.description: A `[jobs.<name>]` in the repo's `jobs.toml` at that commit, or in the routine directory's when it has a routine.

args.description: Appended to the job's `run` command from `jobs.toml`.

memory.description: MiB the container may use, and the runner reserves for it. Null: `jobs.toml`'s, within the 1024 MiB a run without one is admitted with.

timeout.description: Seconds before the runner stops it and it fails. Null: `jobs.toml`'s.

labels.description: Labels as Kubernetes writes them. On a run, what a runner must have, every key with that value; on a runner, what it has.

for.description: What the run was for, as `GET /runs?for=<kind>:<id>` lists it.

kind.description: What asked for the run: an approval-service batch or change, a work-tracker item, or a worker.

routine.description: Where the job's steps live, when not in its own repo: `job` is read from `<dir>/jobs.toml` in `repo` at `commit`, and the run's own `repo` and `commit` are its target, the package checked out at `/work` beside the routine. Only a runner that says it `can` run a `routine` claims it.

commit.description: The routine repo's commit, as a full lowercase sha: the runner checks out exactly this.

host.description: The machine it must run on, as a runner's `hostId`: claimed only by that machine's runner, and only one that says it `can` run `host` runs, which runs it on the host itself, with the host's user services, if that host's config lets it. Null: any runner that fits.

anyOf.description: The machine it runs on: its worker-host's `host_id`, by default the hostname.

tools.name: list_runs
tools.title: List runs
tools.description: Returns runs matching every filter given, newest first.

state.description: `pending` until a runner claims it, `running` on that runner, then `succeeded`, `failed` or `canceled`, which it never leaves.

submittedBy.description: Only the runs submitted with this `claimed-by`, as `submittedBy` records it.

for.description: `<kind>:<id>`, e.g. `item:28af81bc-…`: only the runs submitted with that `for`.

limit.description: At most this many, newest first.

tools.name: get_run_log
tools.title: Read a run's log
tools.description: Returns the log from byte `offset`, at most 1 MiB, with the log's size so far and the run's state. Empty when `offset` is the log's size: call again later from there while the run is `pending` or `running`.

offset.description: The byte to read from; default 0.

tools.name: cancel_run
tools.title: Cancel a run
tools.description: A pending run ends `canceled` at once. A running one is marked `cancelRequested`: its runner is told on its next log append, stops it, and reports it `canceled`.

tools.name: list_runners
tools.title: List runners
tools.description: Returns every registered runner, most recently seen first, with its labels and host.
